pr_title: LE Audio: Broadcast source subgroup support
pr_body:
Updates the BAP broadcast API to support setting multiple subgroups as well as BIS specific codec configuration data. 

Depends on https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/49872
fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/47243
fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/47242
pr_comments: LGTM.  Maybe it would be nice to have some different metadata on the subgroups (e.g. lang = english/spanish as the spec example) + a broadcast_audio_sink sample to handle it (e.g. select the one with spanish).  Can be another PR.

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Add support for stream specific codec configurations for broadcast source
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The BASE supports having unique codec configurations per stream in a broadcast source, but the current API does not support that. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add support for supplying a `struct bt_codec` codec configuration _per_ stream, instead of only per subgroup. This is used to e.g. give a stream a specific location (e.g. LEFT or RIGHT). 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2520413/177125139-edfda023-b501-4476-ba9b-903b1a2637cc.png)

review_comments: magic number

It's just a buffer large enough to hold some data. 

Would you like me to modify the value to the specific exact value needed (which would then need an update every time we modify the number of streams, the codec configuration or the metadata)?
You're right, it does not make sense
can `subgroup->streams` be empty?
No, a broadcast source cannot exist without at least 1 stream

It looks a bit odd I must say. Does it make sense to define structure this way? It might be empty. Is the implementation usable if CONFIG_BT_CODEC_MAX_DATA_COUNT is 0 or not defined?

Good catch. There was actually a place missing a guard for this. 
I added the guard, but maybe we need to revisit this definition. 

Do you have any suggestions?
Not really. Let's leave it as it is. Sorry for late response
Seems it's not needed to call this function, as `source` has not been modified by this function

`source` gets modified in a few lines below: 
```c
sys_slist_append(&source->subgroups, &subgroup->_node);
```

And several other times further below. Keep in mind that this is also done in a loop.
It's not entirely clear to me, but is it here it would be possible to set e.g. language metadata as well?
The metadata parameters are supplied in the `codec` parameter on the next line, along with the codec configuration parameters
can `subgroup->streams` be empty?
No, a broadcast source cannot exist without at least 1 stream
I know that you move code only. But I feel we need to rename this to e.g. `bt_audio_stream_init`. The reason is that there is no registration actually

It's not the same, in the examples you mentioned there is actual callback registration, e.g. `bt_conn_cb_register` makes the `struct bt_conn_cb` to be appended to the callback lists, `bt_conn_auth_cb_register` registers `struct bt_conn_auth_cb` where can be just one registered.

In your case, the application provides uninitialized `struct bt_audio_stream *stream` object and is obliged to **initialize** the `ops` member by calling `bt_audio_stream_cb_register`. If the app won't do that, the object is simply unusable

That is a fair point. 

The audio stream callbacks (or ops) are more in line with the ISO or L2CAP channel ops, which are actually never registered with a function. 

This is one the problems I've always had with both the ISO, L2CAP and `bt_audio_stream` APIs: Some fields in the structs are expected to be set directly by the upper layers, and some are expected to be controlled by the stack. This is not only not documented, but even if it was, it would be hard to keep track of. 

Ideally all the fields are the owner's to control (perhaps with exception like `sys_snode_t _node;` which are always stack controlled), or none of them are (and in which case, the struct should be opaque/abstract). 

As long as `bt_audio_stream` is this weird combination of both, it's hard to define a proper API for it. If we want `bt_audio_stream` to follow the APIs of ISO and L2CAP, then we should simply remove `bt_audio_stream_cb_register`
